skill.description: Manage marketing project memory across sessions with hot cache, archive, decision provenance, and privacy cleanup workflows.
skill.summary: Manage cross-session marketing memory with controlled updates and privacy-aware cleanup.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are markdown backticks, repository-relative links, or memory path names, not executable code or path traversal. The skill does include scoped external command examples and confirmed purge workflows that can inspect, delete, or anonymize project memory files. A contextual privacy risk remains because personal data storage relies on user-controlled lawful-basis and cleanup practices.

remediation.issue: External command examples accept entity names.
remediation.suggestion: Show safer command forms with argument separators before user-controlled patterns, and require preview before execution.

remediation.issue: The purge workflow can modify multiple memory files.
remediation.suggestion: Keep mandatory confirmation, report matched paths, and recommend backup or diff review before destructive edits.

remediation.issue: Personal data handling is advisory rather than enforced.
remediation.suggestion: Add a required checklist before saving third-party personal data and before closing purge requests.

remediation.issue: Relative documentation links trigger path traversal scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that parent-directory links are documentation references and not runtime file traversal inputs.

content.value_statement: Marketing teams lose context when campaign facts, decisions, and audit outputs scatter across sessions. This skill organizes memory tiers, updates hot cache, and guides privacy-aware cleanup.
actual_capabilities: Creates and maintains memory folders for campaign facts, decisions, audits, and glossary entries.
Keeps hot cache within line and size limits with archive recommendations.
Looks up project context across hot cache, glossary, active memory, and archive files.
Routes outputs from SEO, influencer, paid ads, and email skills into defined memory paths.
Guides confirmed GDPR and CCPA working-tree purge logs with scope limitations.
limitations: Does not erase git history or external copies of stored personal data.
Does not replace legal review for GDPR, CCPA, or other privacy obligations.
Depends on the user to provide tool data when integrations are unavailable.
Can edit project memory files, so users should review changes before commit.

use_cases.title: Maintain campaign context
use_cases.description: Keep current priorities, decisions, and glossary terms available across sessions.

use_cases.title: Refresh audit memory
use_cases.description: Save ranking, competitor, content, ad, or email audit outputs into the right memory tier.

use_cases.title: Document privacy cleanup
use_cases.description: Review matches, confirm changes, and record working-tree erasure actions without storing raw subject names.

prompt_templates.title: Set up memory
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up marketing memory for [project name]. Ask for missing inputs before writing files.

prompt_templates.title: Refresh hot cache
prompt_templates.scenario: Update saved context after a completed analysis.
prompt_templates.prompt: Update hot cache after [analysis type]. Show planned changes and ask before saving.

prompt_templates.title: Run hygiene review
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate maintenance for an existing memory folder.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review memory health. Check hot-cache size, stale files, missing frontmatter, and archive candidates.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare privacy purge
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced cleanup for a named data subject or entity.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a GDPR or CCPA working-tree purge for [entity]. List matches, request confirmation, and write a subject-free log.

output_examples.input: Run memory health check for this project.
output_examples.output: The report lists hot-cache size, stale files, missing frontmatter, archive candidates, and recommended next actions.

output_examples.input: Update memory after the competitor analysis from today.
output_examples.output: The skill proposes hot-cache updates, archive entries, affected paths, and a short handoff summary for review.

output_examples.input: Prepare a purge for a named data subject.
output_examples.output: The skill searches memory paths, presents matches, asks for confirmation, and records a subject-free purge summary.

best_practices: Ask before writing, deleting, or anonymizing memory files.
Keep hot cache short and reserve archives for historical context.
Record decision provenance and treat non-user-approved decisions as advisory.
anti_patterns: Do not store personal data without a lawful basis.
Do not present working-tree redaction as full history erasure.
Do not copy large audit tables into monthly archive summaries.

faq.question: What does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It manages campaign memory files, hot cache updates, archives, decisions, glossary entries, and cleanup workflows.

faq.question: Does it run marketing audits itself?
faq.answer: No. It stores and organizes outputs from other audit, research, and campaign skills.

faq.question: Can it delete personal data completely?
faq.answer: No. It can guide working-tree redaction, but git history and external copies need separate handling.

faq.question: Does it need connected tools?
faq.answer: No. Connected SEO or analytics tools help, but the skill can ask the user for missing data.

faq.question: Where does it write files?
faq.answer: It writes under project memory paths such as hot cache, audits, monitoring, glossary, and archives.

faq.question: How should teams review changes?
faq.answer: Teams should inspect the proposed paths, confirm sensitive edits, and review file diffs before commit.
